decisions.statement: A tracker counts the requests begun and not yet ended.
A fresh tracker counts nothing.
Beginning a request raises the count.
Ending a request lowers the count.
An end met while the count is zero leaves the count at zero.
A count never falls below zero.
An idle wait asked for while the count is zero reports the tracker idle.
An idle wait asked for while the count is zero arms no timer.
An idle wait resolves on the end that brings the count to zero.
Every idle wait a tracker has resolves on that same end.
An idle wait resolving on an end reports the tracker idle.
An idle wait outliving its span reports the tracker busy.
An idle wait is resolved the first time and never again.
A resolved idle wait is taken out of the waiting a tracker has.
A resolved idle wait stops the timer that wait armed.
A timer firing while that timer is being armed is stopped once the arming returns.
The timers are handed in so a test needs no wait.
The real timer is unreferenced so a pending wait holds no process up.
A caller that begins a request ends that request on the paths a request ends by.
Nothing here knows the body a request carries.
Nothing here reads a clock.
Nothing here writes a line.
Nothing under this domain asks a tracker for an idle wait.
A request begun after an idle wait resolved leaves that wait resolved.
A tracker counts every request alike rather than counting each path apart.
The old tracker at `tools/lib/model-gateway/gateway.ts` never stopped its timer.

definition: the requests a gateway has taken in and not yet answered
